Head_and_Face: Bill is bright crimson red with a distinctive white transverse band near the tip and a blackened nail at the extremity.
Bill surface is smooth and glossy.
Eyes are red or grey-red with a prominent bare orbital skin patch.
Body_and_Plumage: Plumage is uniformly deep black to dark grey-brown with a velvety matte texture.
Primary and secondary flight feathers exhibit white iridescent edges visible during wing-spreading.
Neck is elongated and gracefully curved, comprising approximately one-third of total body length.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs and webbed feet are dark grey to black with thick, flattened toes.
Characteristic S-curved neck posture when swimming with body held low in water.
Broad, powerful wings creating a boat-like silhouette.

Head_and_Face: Prominent elongated tusks protrude from the oral region.
In elephants, tusks are cream-to-white, smooth, curving outward and upward.
In wild boar, tusks are curved, blade-like projections from upper and lower jaws.
Wild boar has an elongated snout with a cartilaginous disc.
Body_and_Plumage: Elephant has thick, deeply wrinkled grey-brown hide with sparse bristly hair.
Elephant ears are large and fan-shaped with prominent venation.
Wild boar has coarse dark brown to black bristly fur with a prominent dorsal ridge.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Elephant exhibits pillar-like limbs supporting enormous body.
Wild boar has stout muscular legs in a robust quadrupedal stance.
Tusk apparatus creates a distinctive silhouette identifiable at distance.

Head_and_Face: Snout is elongated, tubular, and hairless with a smooth leathery surface.
Snout terminates in a small slit-like mouth and nostrils.
Eyes are minute and partially obscured by facial fur.
Body_and_Plumage: Compact, ovoid body covered in dense protective spines.
Spines are cream-to-dark brown, rigid and sharply pointed, arranged in rows interspersed with coarse brown fur.
Coloration varies from pale cream spines with dark fur to uniformly dark brown.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Forelimbs are short and muscular with five digits bearing thick, curved dark claws.
Hind limbs are similarly structured but oriented rearward.
Tail is short and conical, often concealed beneath body spines.
Body held close to ground with a hedgehog-like defensive appearance.

Head_and_Face: Broad, flat, leathery bill resembling a duck's beak.
Bill surface is smooth and flexible, covered in tiny dark dots (electroreceptive organs).
Bill coloration is dark grey to black with a slightly lighter ventral surface.
Eyes and ears are small and positioned laterally.
Body_and_Plumage: Streamlined, fusiform body covered in dense, waterproof fur.
Rich dark brown dorsal surface transitioning to lighter grey-brown ventrally.
Fur texture is plush and velvety with a silvery sheen when wet.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Feet are fully webbed (palmate) with dark keratinous claws on forelimbs.
Tail is broad, flat, and beaver-like, covered in coarse fur.
Characteristic swimming posture with body submerged and bill trailing forward.

Head_and_Face: Head is small relative to body with large, mobile ears that are rounded or slightly pointed.
Ear coloration often contrasts with body fur.
Eyes are large and dark, positioned laterally.
Body_and_Plumage: Fur is dense and soft, ranging from grey-brown to reddish-brown.
Species-specific patterning includes pale lateral stripes, dark dorsal streaks, or white facial markings.
Some species exhibit brightly colored fur on limbs or rump.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Hind legs are disproportionately large compared to forelimbs, adapted for hopping.
Thick, muscular tail used for balance and as a fifth limb during slow movement.
Forelimbs are short with five distinct digits and small claws.
Feet covered in short fur with dark keratinous claws.

Head_and_Face: Head is broad and domed with a prominent, large leathery nose that is black and smooth.
Nose width is proportionally large relative to head size with a distinctive textured surface pattern.
Ears are large, rounded, and heavily furred with long white tufted hair extending from the margins.
Ear coloration contrasts with grey body fur.
Eyes are small, dark, and widely spaced.
Body_and_Plumage: Stocky, tailless body with a rounded silhouette.
Body fur is dense, woolly, and plush with uniform grey to grey-brown coloration.
Ventral fur is lighter (white to cream) with a distinctive white chest patch.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Forelimbs are muscular with five digits; first two digits are opposable to the remaining three.
Claws are long, curved, and dark keratinous.
Characteristically slumped posture when seated in tree forks with limbs wrapped around branches.

Head_and_Face: Head is broad and blunt with a short, wide snout covered in sparse whiskers.
Nose is large, leathery, and hairless with a smooth grey-brown surface.
Eyes are small and dark, positioned laterally.
Ears are short, rounded, and partially concealed by fur.
Body_and_Plumage: Compact, barrel-shaped body resembling a small bear or badger.
Fur is coarse and bristly, ranging from sandy brown to grey-brown to black.
Fur texture is harsh and wiry with minimal undercoat.
Tail is vestigial and nearly invisible beneath body fur.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Short, muscular limbs nearly equal in length, creating a horizontal backline.
Feet are broad with five digits bearing thick, flattened dark claws.
Characteristic squat posture when stationary with limbs tucked beneath the barrel-shaped body.
Body held close to ground with a slow, shuffling walk.

Head_and_Face: Bell margin is lined with numerous short tentacles or sensory structures appearing as small dark dots.
Body_and_Plumage: Bell is hemispherical to saucer-shaped with a smooth, glossy, gelatinous surface.
Bell exhibits varying degrees of transparency.
Coloration ranges from clear/transparent to milky white, blue, pink, or purple.
Oral arms hang from underside, typically four in number, with frilly, ruffled margins.
Oral arms are translucent with a mucous coating.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tentacles extend from the bell margin, thin, filamentous, and translucent.
Tentacles exhibit a trailing, undulating appearance in water.
Radial symmetry with a pulsating swimming form.

Head_and_Face: Oral disc at the apex is circular and flat.
Oral disc surrounded by one or more concentric rings of tentacles numbering from dozens to hundreds.
Central mouth is a slit-like opening at the center of the oral disc.
Body_and_Plumage: Body column is cylindrical with a smooth, sticky surface.
Column may exhibit vertical striations or tubercles.
Coloration is highly variable including green, brown, pink, purple, orange, or white.
Often displays contrasting longitudinal stripes or spots.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tentacles are cylindrical, tapering, and retractable.
Tentacle coloration often contrasts with the column and may exhibit banding or tip coloration.
Tentacle surface is smooth and mucous-coated with a slightly translucent appearance.
Can retract tentacles and oral disc into the column when disturbed, creating a hemispherical mound.

Head_and_Face: Surface exhibits a distinctive convoluted, maze-like pattern of raised ridges separated by deep furrows.
Pattern resembles the gyri and sulci of a mammalian brain.
Body_and_Plumage: Hemispherical to boulder-shaped colony form.
Coloration is typically brown, tan, olive-green, or grey.
Darker furrows and lighter ridges create a high-contrast topographic pattern.
Surface texture is rough, granular, and abrasive.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Ridge surfaces covered in thousands of minute polyp structures appearing as tiny pores or pits.
Overall colony form is amorphous and dome-shaped.
Furrow-ridge pattern is consistent across the entire colony surface.
